nodes.summary: Fix a natural number $\ell$. The sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is defined recursively: $a_n$ is the least natural number greater than $\ell$ that differs from $a_i$ and from $a_i + i + \ell + 1$ for every $i < n$. Writing $b_i = a_i + i + \ell + 1$, this says that $a_n$ is the least natural number outside $\{0, 1, \dots, \ell\} \cup \{a_i, b_i : i < n\}$; in particular $a_0 = \ell + 1$ and $b_0 = 2\ell + 2$.

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ be a natural number, let $a_n$ be the least natural number $m > \ell$ with $m \ne a_i$ and $m \ne b_i$ for all $i < n$, where $b_i = a_i + i + \ell + 1$ (the mex sequences of $K^\ell$). This is the set of positions $(x, y)$ of natural numbers with $x + y \le \ell$ (the terminal positions of $K^\ell$), together with the pairs $(a_n, b_n)$ and $(b_n, a_n)$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Predicted P-positions of $K^\ell$
